rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 40, Step 1, question 1: "If, in 2025: 3 or more children who have valid SSNs lived with you, is the amount on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 11b, less than $61,555 ($68,675 if married filing jointly)? ... No. STOP You can’t take the credit." i1040gi p. 46, Worksheet A: "Use this worksheet only if you answered “No” to Step 5, question 2. Otherwise, use Worksheet B." i1040gi p. 48, Worksheet B, line 6. The line validates but the reply does not (The reply is invalid: eic.h_qc_conditions, h_step34_ok, h_income_below_limit, h_earned_below_limit, h_wsb_below_limit, h_step5_ok and h_below_threshold put bare `all:` mappings inside `any:` lists without `op: test` ("malformed expression (project schema)"), and eic.h_qc_conditions also carries an empty `all`; triage executed nothing (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/eic.deepseek.json`, state invalid)). By reading: it copies Step 5 earned income onto line 1 on every return, with no shown_when, so it shows an amount after every STOP and gives a Worksheet B filer Step 5 earned income instead of Worksheet B line 6 (as the previous round, e.g. classm.eic.3 $12,259.68 / $13,709.00, stage14.eic.wsb_loss $8,000.00 / $10,000.00). Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: finding; the candidate encodes a skipped line 5 as zero and the project does not. i1040gi p. 46, Worksheet A, line 4: "Are the amounts on lines 3 and 1 the same? Yes. Skip line 5; enter the amount from line 2 on line 6." and line 5: "... is the amount on line 3 less than $10,620 ($17,730 if married filing jointly)? ... Yes. Leave line 5 blank; enter the amount from line 2 on line 6." executable-triage-v1 (triage/eic.deepseek.json; same bank, 1,717 comparisons): 188 differ - 92 value (project positive, candidate 0.00) and 95 project-unknown, every one on a return where line 4 is Yes or line 5 is to be left blank (derivation: eic.line4 True or eic.line5_blank True on all 187), e.g. classm.f2441.4 (line 4 Yes, project 1,709.00), classm.eic.3 (line 4 Yes, 5,490.00), classm.eic.1 (line 3 2,137.00 below $10,620, 723.00), classm.asset.4 / classm.s1.2 (negative AGI: "no band", no value). Line 6 does not read line 5 there, so the credit is unaffected. Under the README skipped-line rule a nonzero amount (or no value) on a line the source says to skip is a defect of the side producing it, here the project. The 1 candidate-refuses (audit.household.filer_under16) is a cited household screen the project also refuses on the return: scope. See eic.findings.md F1.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; on the reply format. The prompt lists the line as printed '6 (eic.line6)' (id eic.line6), beside '6 (eic.wsb_6)'; the reply printed it '6', so the comparison found no line (MISSING) and triage could not run it. By reading, it would also be wrong on the merits: i1040gi p. 40, Step 1, question 1: "If, in 2025: 3 or more children who have valid SSNs lived with you, is the amount on Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 11b, less than $61,555 ($68,675 if married filing jointly)? ... No. STOP You can’t take the credit." i1040gi p. 46, Worksheet A: "Use this worksheet only if you answered “No” to Step 5, question 2. Otherwise, use Worksheet B." The reply's eic.line6 is the Worksheet A choice of line 2 or the smaller of lines 2 and 5 with no Steps 1 to 5 and no shown_when, figured from a line 1 that ignores Worksheet B, so it shows a credit after every STOP (as its eic.credit, e.g. stage9.eic.no_child.over65 $308.00 where the project hides line 6). Project stands.

The candidate's test is any person's Worksheet B self-employment amount nonzero (person.eic_se_has) or any Schedule C (person.sc_count); the project's is a Schedule C (eic.sc_count > 0), clergy, church employee and statutory employee income being refused by scope.schedule1. A Schedule C with a loss is self-employment either way, so the second disjunct is the project's; the first adds nothing the second does not hold, as person.eic_se_has is figured from the person's Schedules C (person.sc_total, or the Schedule SE Part 1 amount when Schedule SE is filed, which in this tool requires a Schedule C). The ruling adjudicates the declaration, not a tax difference.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; i1040gi p. 41, Step 3, question 3: "Are you a married taxpayer whose filing status is married filing separately or head of household? Yes. Continue No. Skip questions 4 and 5; go to question 6"; question 6: "No. Check the box in the Dependents section that discusses the special rule for separated spouses" (amb.2025.separated_spouses_box). The line and its helpers validate but the reply does not (The reply is invalid: eic.h_qc_conditions, h_step34_ok, h_income_below_limit, h_earned_below_limit, h_wsb_below_limit, h_step5_ok and h_below_threshold put bare `all:` mappings inside `any:` lists without `op: test` ("malformed expression (project schema)"), and eic.h_qc_conditions also carries an empty `all`; triage executed nothing (`reviews/2025/transcription/triage/eic.deepseek.json`, state invalid)). By reading: it reads the filing status alone (eic.h_mfs_or_hoh), so an unmarried head of household with a qualifying child, who answers No to question 3 and has no spouse, gets the box if eic.same_home is answered no, and it skips Steps 1 and 2 (a filer above the Step 1 limit can get the box); its qualifying child count requires a valid SSN, which Step 3 question 1 does not. Project stands.
